issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping or flaring between gears, harsh or late shifts, a whining noise, the O/D OFF light flashing, or no reverse. Some cars lose drive completely on the road.
issues.why: The automatic transmissions in these 626s have a poor track record, and many owners and mechanics blame overheating of the fluid for wearing out the internal clutches. Failures are most often reported between about 50,000 and 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell right away; dark or burnt fluid is a bad sign. If it is slipping or will not engage, avoid hard driving and have a transmission shop diagnose it before damage gets worse.

issues.t: O/D OFF light flashing after highway driving
issues.sym: The O/D OFF light on the dash starts flashing after a long highway drive or in hot weather, and shifting may feel different.
issues.why: The transmission computer stores a fault code (P1783) when the transmission fluid gets too hot. Mazda issued a service bulletin about this condition. Repeated overheating shortens the life of the transmission.
issues.next: Have the code read and the fluid checked and changed if it is dark. Ask about an auxiliary transmission cooler if you tow, drive in heat, or do long highway trips.

issues.t: Ignition switch can overheat and smoke (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the steering column when you start the car, or the starter keeps running after the engine has started.
issues.why: Grease inside the ignition switch can carbonize over time and let current flow between the contacts, overheating the switch. Mazda recalled 1993-1998 626s (campaign 15V674) and replaces the switch for free.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If you smell smoke or the starter stays engaged, stop driving and contact a Mazda dealer. Check your VIN for this open recall.

issues.t: Airbags can deploy in a minor underbody bump (recall)
issues.sym: The front airbags go off after a low-speed hit to the underside of the car, such as striking a curb, a rock or a deep pothole.
issues.why: The airbag sensor module on 1996 626s could treat a minor underbody impact as a crash. Mazda recalled about 213,000 cars to reprogram the sensor unit (campaign 98V249).
issues.next: Have a Mazda dealer confirm the recall reprogramming was done. If the airbag light is on, have the system checked.

issues.t: Timing belt tensioner spring can break (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can suddenly stall while driving. You may not notice anything before it happens.
issues.why: An outside spring on the timing belt tensioner could break and get caught in the timing belt. Mazda recalled about 31,000 cars built from August 1997 to August 1998 (campaign 00V134).
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer to check whether the tensioner was inspected or replaced. Because the timing belt drives the engine valves, keep up with timing belt changes too.

issues.t: Brake fluid reservoir cap missing vent holes (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing obvious at first; over time the brakes may feel less effective.
issues.why: Some brake master cylinder reservoir caps were made on a worn tool and lacked vent holes, letting pressure in the reservoir drop and possibly reducing braking. Mazda recalled them (campaign 00V074).
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the reservoir cap and replace it if it is one of the bad ones. It is a quick, free fix.

issues.t: Audio unit short can overheat a speaker (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from a speaker or the dash area.
issues.why: A short circuit at one set of terminals on certain audio units could overheat a speaker and in rare cases start a fire. Mazda recalled about 73,000 cars (campaign 98V243).
issues.next: If you smell burning from the audio system, turn it off and have a dealer check whether the recall was done.

issues.t: Engine may stall while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off unexpectedly while driving, which can make steering and braking harder.
issues.why: Mazda recalled about 20,000 early 1998 626s in December 1997 for a condition that could make the engine stall (campaign 97V228).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a Mazda dealer run your VIN to confirm the recall work was done.

issues.t: Rough idle or stalling from idle air control valve
issues.sym: Idle speed that is too low, hunts up and down, surges when the A/C cycles, or the engine stalls when you stop.
issues.why: The idle air control (bypass air) valve gets dirty or fails with age, so the computer can no longer hold a steady idle. Worn plugs, a weak coil or a vacuum leak can cause similar symptoms.
issues.next: Have codes read and the idle air valve tested and cleaned before replacing parts. Rule out vacuum leaks and ignition parts at the same time.

issues.t: Vacuum leak causing rough running
issues.sym: Rough or high idle, hesitation, a hissing sound under the hood, and a check engine light with lean codes.
issues.why: Rubber vacuum hoses and intake connections harden and crack with age, letting unmetered air into the engine and upsetting the fuel mixture.
issues.next: A smoke test quickly finds the leak. Replacing cracked hoses is usually a simple fix.

issues.t: Low EGR flow code from clogged passages
issues.sym: Check engine light with an EGR flow code (P0400 or P0401), sometimes with rough idle or pinging under load.
issues.why: Carbon builds up in the small exhaust gas recirculation passages in the V6 intake, blocking the flow even when the EGR valve itself works.
issues.next: Have the EGR valve tested first. If it is fine, the passages need to be cleaned, which means removing the throttle body and intake manifold.

issues.t: Check engine light with oxygen sensor codes P1131/P1132
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes P1131 or P1132, often with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Mazda issued service bulletins for these codes on 1998-1999 626s. Some cars set them repeatedly even after oxygen sensors were replaced.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or shop to check for the bulletin fix before buying parts. Replace an oxygen sensor only if testing shows it is slow or dead.

issues.t: Rough idle and hesitation with check engine light
issues.sym: The 4-cylinder idles roughly and hesitates when you accelerate, with the check engine light on.
issues.why: Mazda released a service bulletin (01500) for this condition on early-built 4-cylinder 626s. Owners also report misfires that come back after plugs and wires are replaced.
issues.next: Have a shop read the codes and check for the bulletin. Also check plugs, wires, coil and vacuum hoses.

issues.t: Coolant leak at engine block heater
issues.sym: Drips of coolant under the front of the car and a slowly dropping coolant level.
issues.why: On 4-cylinder cars fitted with a block heater, coolant can seep where the heater sits in the engine block. Mazda covered this in a service bulletin.
issues.next: Find the source of the leak before topping up again. Low coolant can lead to overheating.

issues.t: Water pump leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips from the front of the engine, a sweet smell, and a coolant level that keeps dropping.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears out with age. Mazda issued a bulletin on how to inspect these pumps for leaks. The pump sits behind the timing belt, so it is usually replaced with the belt.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure tested. Replace the pump, timing belt and tensioner together to avoid paying for the same labor twice.

issues.t: Coolant reservoir cracks and leaks
issues.sym: Coolant puddles near the overflow bottle or the level drops with no obvious leak elsewhere.
issues.why: The plastic coolant reservoir cracks with age and heat. One V6 owner reported replacing it several times.
issues.next: Replace the cracked bottle and refill with the right coolant. Check that the radiator cap holds pressure.

issues.t: Clutch pedal sinks and will not release
issues.sym: On manual-transmission cars, the clutch pedal goes soft or sinks to the floor and the car is hard to put in gear.
issues.why: The seals inside the clutch master or slave cylinder wear out, so hydraulic pressure leaks away.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid reservoir for low fluid and look for leaks at the cylinders. Rebuilding or replacing the cylinder is usually enough.

issues.t: Groaning from front strut mounts in turns
issues.sym: A groan, creak or squeak from the front when turning the steering at low speed or over bumps.
issues.why: The front strut mounts and their bearings wear out, and Mazda also issued a bulletin for steering squeak noises.
issues.next: Have the strut mounts and struts inspected. Mounts are usually replaced along with the struts.

issues.t: Musty smell from A/C vents
issues.sym: A musty or mildew smell when the A/C or fan first comes on.
issues.why: Moisture stays on the A/C evaporator and mold grows on it. Mazda has issued several bulletins on this odor.
issues.next: Have the evaporator cleaned and the cabin drain checked. Running the fan without A/C for a few minutes before parking helps.

issues.t: Sunroof stuck, binding or noisy
issues.sym: The sunroof does not open or close, moves slowly, or makes grinding noises.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins for sunroofs that bind or stop working on these years, mainly from the track and drive parts.
issues.next: Have the tracks cleaned and lubricated first. If the motor is bad it needs to be replaced.

issues.t: Horn not working or stuck on
issues.sym: The horn does not sound, or it sounds on its own and will not stop.
issues.why: Mazda issued a service bulletin (00800) for horns that stop working or stay on, related to the horn switch and its circuit.
issues.next: If it is stuck on, pull the horn fuse and have the switch and relay checked.

issues.t: Shifter can leave Park without pressing the brake
issues.sym: You can move the shift lever out of Park without your foot on the brake pedal.
issues.why: The brake shift interlock, which should lock the lever in Park until the brake is pressed, can be disabled by mistake. Mazda issued a bulletin (0400502) covering 1996-2002 626s.
issues.next: Have the interlock checked and repaired. Until then, always press the brake firmly before shifting.

issues.t: Rear drum brake squeal
issues.sym: A high-pitched squeal from the rear wheels when braking.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin (00199) for rear drum brake squeal on early-built cars, linked to the brake shoe lining.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected and fitted with updated shoes if needed.

issues.t: Windshield wipers stop working
issues.sym: The wipers stop partway or stop working, then may come back after a while.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin (003/97G) for wiper motors that quit because the circuit breaker in the motor trips.
issues.next: Have the wiper motor and linkage checked. A binding linkage can make the breaker trip.
